insightOfTheDay.title: The Super Bowl Licensing Window Is NOW
insightOfTheDay.body: ZipChair published Seahawks Super Bowl LX Champions products within hours of the game. Secretlab, DXRacer, and Mavix have ZERO capability to sell licensed championship merchandise. This is a 2-4 week window of pure organic demand — fans actively searching for championship gear. Recommendation: Boost ad spend 3x on Seahawks products, create urgency with 'Limited Championship Edition' messaging, and cross-sell to existing Seahawks customers in the database.

weeklyInsights.title: Price War Brewing in $400-$500 Segment
weeklyInsights.body: Three competitors (Secretlab TITAN Evo, DXRacer Craft, Mavix M5) now cluster in the $399-$474 range after sales. ZipChair's Xpression Pro at $349-$399 is actually the value leader. Position accordingly.

weeklyInsights.title: Ergonomic Positioning Gap
weeklyInsights.body: Mavix is winning the 'ergonomic gaming chair' narrative with mesh-back designs and 91% positive sentiment on ergonomics. ZipChair should consider a mesh-back option for the gaming line to compete.

weeklyInsights.title: DXRacer Brand Perception Declining
weeklyInsights.body: DXRacer's NPS (38) is lowest among competitors. 'Outdated design' is their top complaint theme. They're vulnerable — their customers are looking for alternatives.

weeklyInsights.title: Secretlab Entertainment vs ZipChair Sports: Parallel Moats
weeklyInsights.body: Secretlab is building an entertainment/gaming IP licensing moat (Diablo, Naruto, Lamborghini). ZipChair owns the sports licensing moat (NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL). These barely overlap today but watch for convergence in esports.
